title: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
subject: English

notes.heading: Word Meanings
points: Protagonist: The main character of a story or novel.
Ardent: Very passionate, enthusiastic, or deeply committed.
Savouring: Enjoying a taste or an experience slowly and fully.
Embarrassed: Feeling self-conscious, awkward, or ashamed in front of others.
Determined: Having a strong, firm decision to achieve something no matter what.
Regret: A feeling of sadness or disappointment about a missed opportunity in the past.
Obstacle: A difficulty or barrier that blocks progress or prevents you from moving forward.
Diligently: Working with great care, effort, and steady focus.
Well-off: Having plenty of money to live a rich and comfortable life.
Overcome: To successfully defeat or deal with a major problem.
Illiterate — Unable to read or write

summary: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read by   Sudha Murty   is a heartwarming autobiographical essay that beautifully illustrates the power of determination, the value of literacy, and the unique bond between a grandmother and her granddaughter. The story is set in a remote village in North Karnataka, where the   twelve-year-old narrator  lives with her grandparents. Her   sixty-two-year-old grandmother, Krishtakka , had never attended school due to her early marriage and societal norms of her youth. Despite being illiterate, the grandmother is an avid fan of a popular weekly Kannada magazine serial titled   Kashi Yatre , written by Triveni. Because she cannot read, her granddaughter reads the latest episode aloud to her every Wednesday afternoon, a routine they both cherish. The story reaches a turning point when the narrator goes away to attend a wedding in a neighboring village for a week. During her absence, the magazine arrives, but the grandmother finds herself completely helpless and unable to decipher the text to know what happens next in the story. This experience leaves her deeply embarrassed and makes her realize the painful dependency brought on by illiteracy, prompting her to understand that wealth is meaningless without the dignity of self-reliance. Upon the narrator’s return, the grandmother tearfully confesses her helplessness and firmly resolves to learn the   Kannada alphabet . She sets a strict deadline for herself: the festival of   Dussehra (Saraswati Puja) . Stepping into the role of a teacher, the young granddaughter eagerly guides her aging student. Proving to be an exceptionally dedicated pupil, the grandmother balances her endless kitchen chores with rigorous practice—reading, writing, and reciting her lessons with relentless willpower. Her hard work pays off brilliantly; when Dussehra arrives, she successfully reads the title of the newly published   Kashi Yatre   novel entirely on her own. In a profoundly moving climax, the grandmother surprises the narrator by touching her twelve-year-old granddaughter’s feet. She explains that she is not bowing to her granddaughter, but rather showing traditional respect to her   Guru (teacher)   who empowered her with the gift of knowledge. The story concludes as a beautiful testament to the fact that learning knows no age limits and that education is the ultimate source of freedom and self-respect.

qa.q: What made the grandmother want to learn to read?
qa.a: The grandmother wanted to learn to read because she loved the novel Kashi Yatre . She depended on her granddaughter to read it to her. When her granddaughter was away, she realised that she could not read it herself and decided to become literate.

qa.q: Why did the grandmother feel ashamed?
qa.a: The grandmother felt ashamed because she was unable to read or write even at the age of sixty-two. She depended on others for reading and realised that education was important for becoming independent.

qa.q: How did the grandmother learn to read?
qa.a: The grandmother learned to read with the help of her granddaughter. She practised the Kannada alphabet every day and worked very hard. Within a few weeks, she was able to read independently.

qa.q: Why did the grandmother touch her granddaughter’s feet?
qa.a: The grandmother touched her granddaughter’s feet as a mark of respect. She considered her granddaughter to be her teacher because she had taught her how to read and write.

qa.q: What was the grandmother’s dream? How did she fulfil it?
qa.a: The grandmother’s dream was to read Kashi Yatre on her own. She fulfilled it by learning the Kannada alphabet from her granddaughter and practising regularly until she could read the novel independently.

qa.q: What values does the story teach us?
qa.a: The story teaches us that there is no age limit for learning. It also highlights the importance of determination, education, self-respect and the loving bond between a grandmother and her granddaughter.

qa.q: Why was the grandmother determined to learn to read?
qa.a: The grandmother wanted to become independent and read her favourite novel without depending on anyone. Her inability to read made her realise the importance of education, which motivated her to learn despite her age.
